Question: A man makes a trip by automobile at an average speed of \(50\) mph. He returns over the same route at an average speed of \(45\) mph. His average speed for the entire trip is:
Solution:
Average speed is total distance divided by total elapsed time. The two legs have equal distances, but the slower return takes longer.

We may calculate using \(450\) miles for each leg: multiplying both actual leg distances by a common positive factor also multiplies both travel times by that factor, leaving the average speed unchanged. This distance makes both times whole numbers:
\[
\text{outbound time}=\frac{450}{50}=9\text{ hours},
\]
\[
\text{return time}=\frac{450}{45}=10\text{ hours}.
\]
The entire journey covers \(900\) miles in \(19\) hours, so its average speed is
\[
\frac{900}{19}=47\frac7{19}\text{ mph}.
\]
The answer is choice A.
